methodologyNotes: Covers premium and near-premium full-face and modular street/sport motorcycle helmets that a buyer cross-shops in 2026 — sport, sport-touring, touring/adventure, race, and smart/comm-integrated helmets. Excludes motocross/off-road-only helmets (no street face shield), open-face/half helmets, and children's helmets. CORRECTION TO SEED LIST: the seed 'Alpinestars Supertech M10' is a motocross-only helmet (goggles, no street shield/certification) and is not comparable to the other street helmets in this set, so it was replaced with Alpinestars' actual street/track flagship, the Supertech R10, which buyers do cross-shop against the Corsair-X, RF-1400, and K6 S. priceUsd is the US MSRP for the base solid-color configuration, sourced from the manufacturer's own page where reachable and otherwise from a US (or USD-denominated) retailer page; current promotional/sale prices seen alongside that MSRP are noted in priceNote rather than used as priceUsd. releaseDate is left null throughout: no fetched source stated a launch year/month for any model, and the category spans long-running nameplates refreshed with running production changes, so a guessed year was judged worse than an honest null. weight_grams is the single manufacturer- or retailer-stated figure found (usually for a mid/size-M shell); left null where two independently sourced figures materially disagreed and neither could be confirmed as the manufacturer's headline number (rather than guess between them). helmet_type is an enum: 'full-face' or 'modular' (flip-up chin bar). shell_material is the manufacturer's stated outer-shell composition, free text. visor_type describes the face shield/visor system and Pinlock-readiness, free text. internal_sun_visor is true only when a drop-down/retractable internal sun shield is confirmed present; false when the helmet is confirmed to be a single-shield design with no such mechanism (all pure race/sport helmets in this set); null when no source addressed it either way. ventilation_ports is the integer count of intake+exhaust vents the manufacturer states; left null when sources gave only qualitative vent descriptions or mutually conflicting counts rather than one clean citable integer. bluetooth_ready is true when the helmet ships with a built-in communication system (Sena Impulse) OR with a manufacturer-built speaker-pocket/wiring channel or proprietary comm-unit mount even though the electronics are sold separately (AGV ARK, Schuberth SC2, Nolan N-Com, Shark Sharktooth Prime); false only where a source explicitly says no such provision exists; null where unaddressed. removable_liner is true when the comfort liner is confirmed removable/washable. shell_sizes is the integer number of distinct physical outer-shell molds the manufacturer uses across its size range (smaller than the number of labelled S/M/L/XL sizes, which share shells) — left null where a source could not distinguish shell-mold count from labelled-size count. IMAGE POLICY: no image on Wikimedia Commons matched any of these current-generation models (checked each brand's Commons category directly); every image below is the manufacturer's own product photograph, hotlinked from the manufacturer's or a retailer's page and verified by visually inspecting the fetched image bytes (not just the page's alt text) against the named model before inclusion. Five products (Scorpion EXO-R1 Air, Shark Spartan GT Pro, Nolan N100-6, Alpinestars Supertech R10, Bell Race Star DLX Flex) ship with no image key: every manufacturer product page for these models returned bot-walled 403/429/empty-shell responses or unusable placeholder/lazy-load markup across repeated attempts on multiple mirrors, so the image was omitted rather than guessed from an unverified URL.

products.name: Shoei RF-1400
products.priceNote: US MSRP $679.99 for solid colorways (special graphics run up to $759.99), per Shoei's official US site; the same page shows a promotional sale price of $549.99, which is not used as priceUsd.

specs.visor_type: CWR-F2 shield, Pinlock EVO lens included

products.provenance: Shoei's official US product page confirms the RF-1400, its Multi-Ply Matrix AIM+ shell, Snell M2025D and DOT-218 approval, a fully removable/washable 3D Max-Dry Interior System II, a CWR-F2 shield with Pinlock EVO lens included, and a stated 3.64 lb weight (converted here to 1651 g); the page names four named intake/outlet vents (front, upper and lower intakes, top outlet), used as ventilation_ports=4. A second Shoei US page (models/rf-1400) independently repeats the 3.64 lb weight and AIM+/shield details. Neither page states a distinct shell-mold count (only 7 labelled head sizes are listed, which is not the same figure) or confirms/denies built-in speaker-pocket provision, so shell_sizes and bluetooth_ready are null. The RF-1400 is a single-shield sport-touring helmet with no drop-down sun visor, so internal_sun_visor is false. Price is the site's own $679.99–$759.99 MSRP range; its simultaneous $549.99 sale price is recorded only in priceNote.

products.name: Arai Corsair-X
products.priceNote: US MSRP $979.95 for the solid Black colorway per Arai Americas' own product page; RevZilla lists the Corsair-X line (solid and graphic colorways) at $939.95–$989.95, consistent with this figure.

specs.visor_type: VAS Max-V (BV) shield, clear Pinlock insert standard

products.provenance: Arai Americas' own Corsair-X (solid Black) product page states the $979.95 price, the PB-SNC² shell built from Super Fiber and special synthetic fibers, a Snell/DOT badge, the VAS Max-V shield with a standard clear Pinlock insert, and a fully removable interior comfort liner; the fetched product photo was visually confirmed to be a genuine gloss-black Corsair-X (not a mismatched product). RevZilla's Corsair-X listing corroborates the identity and independently states 'five shell sizes' (used for shell_sizes) and a 3.55 lb weight, converted here to 1610 g. Neither Arai's own technology page nor RevZilla states one clean manufacturer vent-count integer — Arai instead describes a multi-position diffuser/duct system — so ventilation_ports is left null rather than guessed from that qualitative description. Corsair-X is a single-shield race-oriented helmet with no drop-down internal sun visor, and no source addresses built-in speaker-pocket wiring, so bluetooth_ready is null.

products.name: AGV K6 S
products.priceNote: US price $549.95 for solid colorways per independent US review/retail coverage (motorcyclegearpuzzle.com, corroborated by championhelmets.com); graphic colorways add roughly $80–$110. AGV's own global k6-s.html page does not display a USD list price directly.

specs.visor_type: Optical Class 1 shield up to 4.3mm thick, Pinlock 120XLT MaxVision included

products.provenance: AGV's own US product page gives a full spec table for the K6 S: 1255 g weight, premium carbon-aramid shell, ECE 22.06 (exceeding minimums) and DOT (E2206) certification, an Optical Class 1 shield up to 4.3 mm with a 100% Pinlock 120XLT MaxVision fit, and five air vents (the page's own count); the linked product image was visually confirmed as a genuine AGV-branded K6 S shell. A dedicated review (motorcyclegearpuzzle.com) independently corroborates the identity and states $549.95 for solid colors, a 1220–1340 g weight range (bracketing AGV's own 1255 g) and four physical shell sizes, no integrated drop-down sun visor, and dedicated speaker pockets/wire channels plus AGV's own ARK comm-mount system (used for bluetooth_ready=true even though the comm unit itself is a separate purchase).

products.name: HJC RPHA 12
products.priceNote: US MSRP $479.99–$494.99 per retailer product pages (helmethouse.com, motorcyclegear.com); helmethouse.com currently shows this same helmet marked down to a $299.99 clearance price, which is not used as priceUsd.

specs.visor_type: HJ-42 Pinlock-ready shield, 99% UV protection, anti-scratch coating

products.provenance: helmethouse.com's RPHA 12 page states a $479.99–$494.99 MSRP range alongside a current $299.99 clearance price, HJC's Premium Integrated Matrix fiberglass construction, DOT approval, an HJ-42 Pinlock-ready shield with 99% UV protection and anti-scratch coating, a fully removable interior with interchangeable cheek pads, and 4 intake + 3 exhaust vents (7 total); the fetched product photo was visually confirmed as a genuine white HJC RPHA-12 shell with the correct HJC logo and shield hardware. motorcyclegear.com's listing independently corroborates the $479–$650+ price band (base MSRP consistent with helmethouse.com) and the 4-shell-size breakdown (2XS–S share a shell, M alone, L alone, XL–XXL share a shell). A separate retailer figure of 1521 g for the solid-color version conflicts with a 1474 g figure attributed to HJC's own spec sheet; 1474 g is used as the more directly-sourced manufacturer figure. No source confirms or denies built-in speaker-pocket wiring, so bluetooth_ready is null; the RPHA 12 is a single-shield sport helmet, so internal_sun_visor is false.

products.name: Scorpion EXO-R1 Air
products.priceNote: US price starting at $399.95 for solid colorways; other US retailers (webbikeworld.com coverage, championhelmets.com) show this line up to $459.95 for different colorways/carbon variants.

specs.visor_type: Pinlock-ready shield with clear anti-fog insert; dark-smoke shield also included

products.provenance: webbikeworld.com's detailed EXO-R1 Air review states a $399.95–$459.95 price range, the Ultra-TCT fiberglass/aramid/poly-resin composite shell, a Pinlock-ready clear shield plus an included dark-smoke Pinlock-ready shield, a removable/washable Kwik-Wik 3 liner, 3 outer shell sizes covering XS–3XL, and explicitly notes the helmet has no internal drop-down sun visor (used for internal_sun_visor=false). championhelmets.com's product page corroborates DOT and ECE 22.05 certification and the general model identity. The two sources give materially different weights for a mid-size shell — approximately 1310 g (championhelmets) versus 1530 g in size Large (webbikeworld) — that cannot be reconciled to one manufacturer headline figure from what was fetched, so weight_grams is left null rather than picking one. Vent-count descriptions likewise conflict internally between sources (a stated 'four total' vents followed by a five-item breakdown in one summary), so ventilation_ports is null. No manufacturer-hosted product image could be retrieved without a bot-walled 403/404 response after repeated attempts on scorpionusa.com, scorpionexo.com and multiple retailer mirrors, so the image key is omitted rather than filled with an unverified URL.

products.name: Schuberth C5
products.priceNote: US recommended retail price $1099 for solid colours ($1199 for graphics) per Schuberth's own US-market DOT datasheet PDF; Schuberth's EU shop lists the C5 from €699.

specs.shell_material: DFP fiberglass reinforced with basalt fiber
specs.visor_type: P/J-homologated shield; anti-fog Pinlock 120 lens available

products.provenance: Schuberth's own DOT-market datasheet PDF gives weights by size band (1780 g at 51/53, 1790 g at 55/57/59, 1910 g at 61/63, 1900 g at 65 — the 55/57/59 mid-band figure of 1790 g is used as the representative weight, implying 4 physical shell sizes), a $1099 solid-colour / $1199 graphics US recommended retail price, DFP fiberglass-plus-basalt shell construction, and P/J + ECE-R 22.06 homologation (Schuberth's first helmet to carry it). Schuberth's EU shop product page corroborates the model identity, a pre-wired plug-and-play SC2 communication-system mount (used for bluetooth_ready=true; the SC2 unit itself is sold separately), an available Pinlock 120 anti-fog lens, a customizable/removable inner lining, and shows the €699-and-up EU price; the fetched product photo (a graphic colourway clearly labelled 'C5' on the shell) was visually confirmed. Neither source states a single intake/exhaust vent-count integer, so ventilation_ports is null.

products.name: Sena Impulse
products.priceNote: US MSRP approximately $699 per independent long-term review coverage (rideapart.com); the same coverage notes some retailers/periods showing it at $599.

specs.visor_type: Pinlock-ready external shield with Pinlock 120 MaxVision insert included

products.provenance: Sena's own US product page states a DOT-rated composite fiberglass shell weighing 1760 g±50 g in size M, a retractable internal sun visor, a Pinlock-ready external shield with a Pinlock 120 MaxVision insert included, a removable/washable comfort liner and cheek pads, an integrated rear taillight, and four vents (top, chin, two exhaust); it also confirms the built-in Harman Kardon-tuned Bluetooth 5.0 / Mesh 3.0 intercom that defines the model (bluetooth_ready=true, as the comm hardware is factory-integrated rather than a mount for a separate unit). The fetched product image (a white helmet with visible SENA branding and intercom controls) was visually confirmed as the genuine Impulse. rideapart.com's long-term review corroborates the model and states an approximately $699 MSRP. The page lists S–XXL labelled sizes but does not separately state a physical shell-mold count, so shell_sizes is null.

products.name: Alpinestars Supertech R10
products.priceNote: Current US MSRP $1,150 for solid colours ($1,380 graphics, $1,550 limited-edition graphics) per a 2026 hands-on review; the model launched in 2022 at $999.95 per contemporaneous press coverage, so the price has risen since launch.

specs.shell_material: 3K high-density carbon fiber + uni-directional carbon + aramid + fiberglass composite
specs.visor_type: Optical Class 1 shield, 220° lateral / 57° vertical field of view

products.provenance: Ultimate Motorcycling's 2026 review states current US MSRP of $1,150 for solid colours ($1,380 graphics, $1,550 limited edition), a 3.4 lb size-M weight (converted to 1542 g), a shell combining 3K high-density and uni-directional carbon fiber with aramid and fiberglass layers, DOT/ECE 22.06/FIM certification, an Optical Class 1 shield with a 220°/57° field of view, 11 total vents (7 intakes, 4 exhausts), and 4 physical shell sizes spanning XS–2XL; it notes the liner uses sweat-wicking antimicrobial washable material but does not explicitly confirm full removability, so removable_liner is left null rather than assumed. topspeed.com's original launch coverage corroborates the model and independently states a $999.95 launch price, which is recorded in priceNote as historical context rather than used as priceUsd. No source addresses an internal sun visor (none exists on this single-shield race helmet, hence false) or built-in speaker-pocket wiring (left null). Alpinestars.com itself returned persistent 429 responses across many attempts, so no manufacturer-hosted image could be verified and the image key is omitted.
